newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo rubber futures rise on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo rubber futures rise on short-covering.

text.p: Tokyo rubber futures ended higher across the board on Friday, as the yen's weaker tendency against the dollar stimulated short-covering by private investors, traders said.
Rubber prices ranged from 0.8 yen to 1.7 yen per kg higher, with benchmark May ending up 1.7 yen at 146.0 yen.

Rainfall in Thailand, which has started to disrupt the rubber tapping process, also provided psychological support to the market. "The key is whether benchmark May will surpass the recent high of 146.7 yen marked on November 26," one trader said.
